name: spinner
description: An indeterminate activity indicator for small areas: inside a button, an input, a status pill. Code-only. The Loading02 icon spinning in currentColor; the same icon Toast uses, so there is one spinner in the system.

sm.when: Inside a pill or beside text-sm copy (PageBusy's Updating pill).

lg.when: Standalone indicator in an empty area.

tokens.note: No token of its own. Inherits the foreground of its container, so it is correct on every Button variant and in both themes.

composition.element: svg (Loading02 from @untitledui/icons); wrapped in span[role=status] when label is passed

accessibility.role: none by default (aria-hidden icon); role=status when label is set
accessibility.screenReader: Silent unless label is passed. Prefer visible text or aria-busy on the loading region.
accessibility.reducedMotion: motion-reduce:animate-none stops the rotation; the static icon remains.

constraints: Small areas only. Known layout -> Skeleton; measurable task -> Progress.
In a button use <Button loading>, never a hand-placed Spinner.
Show only after 300ms and keep at least 500ms (useDelayedLoading) - Button loading and PageBusy already do this.
One spinner per busy thing - not in the button and the area it updates.
Do not override its colour to signal state; it inherits.

useCases: A button whose action is in flight (via Button loading)
A combobox or search input fetching results
The Updating pill while a page refreshes (inside PageBusy)

comparedTo.situation: A region's layout is known while its data loads
comparedTo.notInstead: spinner (a spinner in a blank box shifts the layout)

comparedTo.situation: The task has a known percentage
A page refreshes data already on screen
comparedTo.notInstead: a spinner placed over the table by hand

comparedTo.situation: A long task the user can leave running
comparedTo.use: toast.loading with Progress in the description
comparedTo.notInstead: a spinning button held for the whole task

openQuestions: Does Spinner get a Figma component, or stay code-only like Skeleton? See docs/handover/loading.md.
notes: 2026-10-07: Added. Promoted from the loading prototype built on the Dashboard (the demo page itself was not kept in the repo; git history 509d2c2). Toast's loading icon now renders this component.

darkMode.notes: currentColor - follows the container's mode-aware foreground. Verified in Storybook: white on the primary button in dark mode.
